source_text:
21.7 ̓Εγὼ
δέ εἰμι σκώληξ. ̔Ως ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ σαρκωθέντος Θεοῦ λέγει, εἰ καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὴν
Θεότητα λαμ βανόμενον, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ φαινόμενον καὶ τὸ ταπεινὸν τῆς σαρκὸς, τό·
̓Εγώ εἰμι ὁ σκωλήξ.
pass_a_gloss: I and am worm. As out-of person of-the having-been-incarnate God he-says, even-if not according-to the Godhead being-taken, but according-to the appearing and the lowly of-the flesh, the: I am the worm.
pass_b_english: He speaks as from the person of the incarnate God, even if it is not taken according to the Godhead, but according to the appearing and the lowliness of the flesh: “I am the worm.”

choices.term: εἰ καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὴν Θεότητα λαμβανόμενον, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ φαινόμενον
choices.english: even if it is not taken according to the Godhead, but according to the appearing
choices.why: The worm-saying is of the incarnate appearing, not the Godhead. Not ‘God is a worm in his deity’.
rejected: God is a worm according to the Godhead
the speaker is only a human prophet

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
